notes.claim: For an incompressible fluid, the flow rate is the same everywhere along the pipe, so it must speed up where the pipe narrows.
When a fluid flows into a narrower channel its speed and kinetic energy increase, and the energy has to come from somewhere: the pressure.
Venturi flow meters work on Bernoulli's principle, using the pressure difference between the pipe and its narrowing to measure flow.
The transition from laminar to turbulent flow is put at Reynolds numbers between about 2000 and 10 000, so its upper edge is contested.
Pitot tubes, venturi meters and orifice plates are used to measure pressure and flow speed.
A sharp-edged orifice has coefficients of velocity, contraction and discharge (Cv, Cc, Cd).
